comparisons.physical_skill: Recessed key insertion, collar tuning, counterholding, and relocking vs guided carrier insertion and cam-handle levering/latching.
comparisons.success_condition: Two safe impact cycles plus setting retention vs insertion depth, handle angle, latch state, and bay/carrier damage limits.
comparisons.reason: Both include a retained final state, but the record tests insertion and cam latching rather than iterative damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Commission and lock a damper vs route a wire around formboard pins and plug it in.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rigid hex-key/collar manipulation with torque control vs deformable-wire routing, regrasping, and connector insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Repeated dynamic stopping and no setting drift vs correct pin-side topology, height limits, plug depth, and release.
comparisons.reason: The manipulation medium and tested ability are materially different.

comparisons.objective: Tune and lock a robot-axis damper vs route a lamp cable clear of a hot plate and place its plug in a holder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine tool engagement, counterholding, collar adjustment, and tightening vs deformable-cable shaping and obstacle avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: Two safe stops with retained setting vs plug seating, cable clearance/height, release, and no hot-zone crossing.
comparisons.reason: The record tests cable routing and safety clearance, not dynamic component commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Commission an adjustable shock absorber vs dispense samples into tubes and mark completed tubes.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key alignment, collar tuning, counterholding, and bounded locking vs pipette pickup, squeezing, dispensing, and tab actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Two repeatable safe impacts and lock retention vs three correctly filled/ticked tubes with the fourth empty and unticked.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful mechanism or success-condition overlap.

comparisons.objective: Commission and lock a damper vs route a wire around formboard obstacles and insert its plug.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rigid tool insertion, collar rotation, and force-limited tightening vs deformable-wire routing, topology control, and plug insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Two safe impact cycles and post-lock stability vs correct routing order/sides, height restriction, connector depth, and release.
comparisons.reason: The record tests deformable routing and insertion, not adjustment or dynamic-response validation.

comparisons.objective: Iteratively tune and lock a shock absorber from observed stopping behavior vs aim a loaded inspection arm to a prescribed angle and lock its indexed clamp.
comparisons.physical_skill: Recessed hex-key engagement, collar rotation, counterholding, repeated test cycles, and bounded relocking vs supporting a loaded arm at angle while tightening a clamp.
comparisons.success_condition: Two repeatable stops within stroke/energy constraints with no bottoming, rebound, overload, or setting drift vs +15-degree retention for two seconds after both grippers withdraw.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest record because both adjust, support, lock, and verify retention. The candidate nevertheless tests iterative dynamic-response calibration and impact safety rather than static pose setting. No separate spec version or numeric clamp tolerances beyond the body summary were available.

comparisons.objective: Commission a robot-axis damper vs extract an out-of-reach cup using two sticks as improvised tongs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine hex-key/collar manipulation and iterative tuning vs bimanual tool pickup, coordinated remote pinching, lifting, and placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Repeated safe stopping and retained setting vs cup removed and standing upright on a target stone for two seconds.
comparisons.reason: The record tests coordinated remote object transport, not mechanism adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Tune and lock a shock absorber vs place cake on the plate identified by number 1.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool alignment, counterholding, fine rotation, and torque control vs visual label selection and simple pick-and-place.
comparisons.success_condition: Two validated impact cycles and no lock drift vs cake resting on the uniquely correct plate.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful objective, physical-skill, or success-condition overlap.

comparisons.objective: Commission and lock a damper vs safely saw a specified-thickness bread slice.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key insertion, collar tuning, counterholding, and bounded tightening vs knife grasping, loaf stabilization, guarded sawing, and cut-depth control.
comparisons.success_condition: Repeated non-bottoming stops and setting retention vs a 1–2 cm released slice with continuous blade-clearance compliance.
comparisons.reason: Shared bimanual stabilization and force control are generic; the mechanisms and measured results differ.

comparisons.objective: Close sprung carton flaps in the required nesting order.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual flap holding and folding against spring return.
comparisons.success_condition: All four flaps closed in order and at rest for 1 s; wrong order fails.
comparisons.reason: Tests coordinated folding and temporary restraint, not tool-driven damper adjustment, locking, or response-based commissioning. Missing explicit damage limits, but the objective is clearly unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Tension, pluck, and release a chalk line to mark a straight line.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain line tension with one hand while vertically plucking with the other.
comparisons.success_condition: Single straight print within position/bow tolerances, followed by reel placement.
comparisons.reason: Shared bimanual force control is generic; it tests compliant-line tension and release, not hex-key engagement, collar rotation, relocking, or iterative impact response.

comparisons.objective: Remove one terminal block from a loose DIN rail without disturbing neighbors.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize the rail while unlatching, lifting, and transferring a small block.
comparisons.success_condition: Target released into tray while adjacent blocks and rail remain within strict disturbance limits.
comparisons.reason: Both use bimanual stabilization, but this tests selective unlatching and extraction rather than rotary adjustment, fastener locking, and dynamic cycle tuning.

comparisons.objective: Remove vitamins and seasonings from a meal table while preserving the place setting.
comparisons.physical_skill: Identify, pick, and place several rigid objects without disturbing nearby items.
comparisons.success_condition: Three hazardous items boxed; plate or mug disturbance zeros the score.
comparisons.reason: Tests semantic selection and collision-free transport, with no tool insertion, threaded release, retained adjustment, or dynamic commissioning. No separate spec versions were present; body scoring was sufficient.

comparisons.objective: Open a folding fan fully and leave it released on its stand.
comparisons.physical_skill: Counterhold one guard stick while sweeping the other around a stiff rivet.
comparisons.success_condition: Fan spread at least 135 degrees, supported and released; full credit also requires arm withdrawal.
comparisons.reason: Although it uses counterholding and controlled rotation, it lacks tool alignment, fastener release/relock, bounded tightening, and adjustment from repeated impact response.

comparisons.objective: Reload a stapler, staple two sheets, and withdraw the finished sheets.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a sprung magazine, insert a staple strip, manipulate sheets, and press the arm.
comparisons.success_condition: Magazine loaded and shut, sheets stapled and removed, objects released, arms withdrawn.
comparisons.reason: Tests sequential insertion and pressing of a consumable mechanism, not unlocking and tuning a damper or validating repeated physical stops.

comparisons.objective: Place a tall canister behind a fence under a low shelf and stand it upright.
comparisons.physical_skill: Constrained tilt insertion, reorientation, and stable release.
comparisons.success_condition: Canister base fully behind fence and upright within 5 degrees for 3 s after release.
comparisons.reason: Tests constrained whole-object placement, not small-tool engagement, collar adjustment, locking torque, or response-guided commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Heat and scrape three paint patches without damaging adjacent glass.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually aim a heat gun while guiding a scraper through softened paint.
comparisons.success_condition: All patches stripped, glass uncracked, tools returned, and arms withdrawn.
comparisons.reason: Shared bimanual tool use is generic; the tested ability is coordinated heating and scraping, not mechanical adjustment and lock retention under repeated impacts.

comparisons.objective: Capture twelve-cell distributed spring preload using a pressure plate and cross-key.
comparisons.physical_skill: Compress a free plate while inserting a separate retaining key, then withdraw both grippers.
comparisons.success_condition: All contacts and retained preload remain correct after release.
comparisons.reason: This is preload transfer by compression and key insertion, not hex-fastener release, fine collar tuning, relocking, or empirical damping adjustment. Body lacks numeric preload/contact thresholds, but the mechanisms remain meaningfully different.

comparisons.objective: Lever a door upward and insert a packer so the door rests on it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Operate a pry bar while sliding and aligning a shim under load.
comparisons.success_condition: Required lift achieved, packer seated, door resting and still, hands released.
comparisons.reason: Tests load lifting and under-load insertion; it does not test rotary calibration, locking torque, or repeated impact-response convergence.

comparisons.objective: Wipe a monitor lead continuously from plug end to clip end.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold one end while executing a continuous, direction-constrained sliding pinch along a compliant lead.
comparisons.success_condition: Required lead length wiped without backtracking, entire lead placed on drape, hands clear.
comparisons.reason: Tests continuous traversal of a compliant cable, not rigid tool insertion, rotary adjustment, locking, or dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Seat a screwdriver in a fitted case and close the lid until its clasp catches.
comparisons.physical_skill: Precision placement followed by hinge closure and spring-clasp engagement.
comparisons.success_condition: Tool seated, lid shut and latched, case stable, arms withdrawn.
comparisons.reason: Clasp engagement is a different one-way closure operation; there is no fastener loosening, collar tuning, witness-torque retention test, or repeated response criterion.

comparisons.objective: Hold an LED flush while applying a soldering-iron tip to one pad, then return the iron.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sustained bimanual micro-alignment of a component and pointed tool.
comparisons.success_condition: Two seconds of uninterrupted pad contact while LED remains flush, with no forbidden contact; iron returned safely.
comparisons.reason: This tests precision holding and timed contact, not hex-key torque, adjustable damping, relocking, or response-based iteration.

comparisons.objective: Simultaneously release two lid latches, lift the lid, and set it aside.
comparisons.physical_skill: Synchronized bimanual latch translation followed by two-handed lifting.
comparisons.success_condition: Both latches released together and lid removed, placed flat, and still without moving the case excessively.
comparisons.reason: Tests simultaneous latch release and extraction, not sequential fastener unlocking, fine rotary adjustment, relocking, or dynamic-cycle validation.

comparisons.objective: Pull a support board to bring an unreachable jar within reach, then basket it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Controlled support-surface pulling followed by object transfer.
comparisons.success_condition: Jar rests in basket; loss from the table fails.
comparisons.reason: Tests means-end retrieval and transport, with none of the candidate's small-tool, locking, calibration, or impact-response requirements.

comparisons.objective: Drain liquid from a pan while retaining dumplings with an ajar lid.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinate lid gap control with pan tilting and pouring.
comparisons.success_condition: Specified drained volume and retained solids, with pan returned upright to the stove.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual force coordination is generic; selective pouring and spill retention do not exercise fastener manipulation, collar tuning, or post-lock dynamic verification.

comparisons.objective: Recover two stranded slot cars while another car continues racing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Assigned-arm pickup and precise insertion into moving-lane conditions while avoiding protected cars.
comparisons.success_condition: Each released car remains lane-engaged and travels 100 mm independently; protected-car contact zeros the score.
comparisons.reason: Tests obstacle-aware recovery and lane insertion, not damper adjustment or retention. Body omits detailed insertion tolerances, but the tested objective is clearly different.

comparisons.objective: Hold a robot-arm bracket while inserting a servo into its close-fit pocket in the correct orientation.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual counterholding, oriented close-clearance insertion, and push-to-seat force.
comparisons.success_condition: Servo correctly oriented and fully seated, bracket set upright, parts released and still.
comparisons.reason: This tests press-fit component assembly; it lacks tool/setscrew engagement, adjustable collar rotation, lock restoration, and iterative dynamic-response tuning.

comparisons.objective: Hold a self-closing gate open while sliding a parcel through to a conveyor.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sustain gate restraint with one hand while pushing a parcel through a constrained opening with the other.
comparisons.success_condition: Parcel reaches run-off plate without gate contact or lifting, gate closes, arms withdraw.
comparisons.reason: Tests simultaneous restraint and transfer through a moving mechanism, not fine adjustment, fastener torque, or repeated carriage-stop commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Register a windowed plate behind an inspection screen despite grasp-related visual occlusion.
comparisons.physical_skill: Visibility-aware grasping, supported regrasp, and precision planar registration.
comparisons.success_condition: Released, supported, stable alignment within 3 mm for full credit or 12 mm for partial credit.
comparisons.reason: Tests active perception and geometric registration, not mechanical unlocking, rotary damping adjustment, relocking, or impact-cycle evaluation. Body supplies only band-level rubric details, but distinction is clear.

comparisons.objective: Match generator speed and phase, then close its breaker at the correct moment.
comparisons.physical_skill: Read an instrument, actuate speed buttons iteratively, and time a final button press.
comparisons.success_condition: Speed matched and first CLOSE press occurs within the specified phase window.
comparisons.reason: Both involve iterative response observation, but this tests instrument-guided button timing and synchronization; the candidate uniquely tests physical tool engagement, collar rotation, lock torque, and impact mechanics.

comparisons.objective: Twist an ice tray to release cubes, invert it into a dish, and restore the tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Opposed bimanual torsion, inversion, pouring, and placement.
comparisons.success_condition: All cubes in dish, tray restored, arms withdrawn and system still.
comparisons.reason: Opposed rotation is only a generic primitive; this tests bulk release and pouring rather than fine retained adjustment and repeated dynamic validation.

comparisons.objective: Open one selected knife-disconnect lever while leaving four neighboring levers closed.
comparisons.physical_skill: Selective small-lever engagement through an over-center snap without disturbing adjacent controls.
comparisons.success_condition: Named lever reaches open angle and remains open; disturbance of other levers is penalized or fails depending on version.
comparisons.reason: Tests selective snap-lever actuation, not tool insertion, fastener loosening/relocking, continuous collar adjustment, or response-guided commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Fit elbows to copper and plastic pipes, first inserting a support insert into the plastic pipe.
comparisons.physical_skill: Material-dependent sequencing and three aligned push-fit insertions.
comparisons.success_condition: Both elbows seated correctly; plastic joint requires prior insert and copper joint must not contain one.
comparisons.reason: Tests rule-governed axial assembly and irreversible ordering, not adjustable damping, locking torque, or repeated impact-cycle convergence.

comparisons.objective: Build two scaffold footings in the order sole board, base plates, then tubes.
comparisons.physical_skill: Place and align multiple load-spreading parts, then insert and stand tubes.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct stacked footing at both marks with positional and tilt tolerances; direct grass placement irreversibly fails.
comparisons.reason: Tests ordered structural placement and tube insertion, not fine rotary adjustment, tool/fastener control, or dynamic response validation.

comparisons.objective: Seat a coolant hose on a barb and tighten its worm-drive clamp.
comparisons.physical_skill: Axial hose insertion, nut-driver seating, repeated regrasping and 3 N·m tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Hose fully home; clamp behind bead and tight; tool and hands released.
comparisons.reason: Shares seated rotary-tool use and bounded tightening, but not unlocking a retained adjustment collar, tuning damping from repeated impacts, or validating travel/rebound and lock drift.

comparisons.objective: Peel a cucumber while leaving both ends intact.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual food stabilization/rotation and force-controlled surface strokes with a swivel peeler.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 44 of 48 patches peeled without gouging, end damage, tool contact, or a fall.
comparisons.reason: Tests continuous blade contact and surface coverage, not fastener engagement, collar adjustment, locking, or dynamic-response commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Mix flour and liquid into dough while steadying a loose bowl.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual bowl stabilization and spoon stirring through granular material.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 95% mixed, with limited spill and bowl tilt.
comparisons.reason: Tests distributed mixing and spill control rather than precision unlocking, rotary tuning, torque-limited relocking, and repeated impact evaluation.

comparisons.objective: Unplug a USB-C cable and stow a spot welder in its holder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual device stabilization, tight plug extraction, placement and reorientation.
comparisons.success_condition: Plug removed by its body and laid down; welder seated upright; arms returned; no dropped parts.
comparisons.reason: Tight connector extraction is meaningfully different from engaging a hex fastener and iteratively tuning and locking a damper.

comparisons.objective: Consolidate shelf stock to create space and shelve a carton.
comparisons.physical_skill: In-contact planar pushing and collision-free carton placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Carton on shelf; all four existing boxes upright, contained and still.
comparisons.reason: Tests spatial rearrangement under containment constraints, with no tool use, retained adjustment, torque control, or dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Back off, square and push a jammed carton through narrowing guides.
comparisons.physical_skill: Nonprehensile pushing, unjamming and planar orientation correction.
comparisons.success_condition: Carton wholly beyond the guides, centered, flat, still and released without bypassing boundaries.
comparisons.reason: The forceful manipulation is planar unjamming, not fine rotary adjustment followed by measured impact-response validation.

comparisons.objective: Insert both ends of a short patch cord into separate tester jacks.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual cable management and constrained connector insertion without unseating the first plug.
comparisons.success_condition: Both plugs at least 15 mm deep, tester units unmoved and plugs released.
comparisons.reason: Tests dual insertion under cable tension; it lacks unlocking, fine setting changes, tightening torque and iterative dynamic observation.

comparisons.objective: Extract one target bottle from a crowded row and place it in a tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Selective grasping and obstacle avoidance among unstable objects.
comparisons.success_condition: Target upright in tray without excessive disturbance or toppling of neighboring bottles.
comparisons.reason: Tests clutter-sensitive extraction rather than tool alignment, rotary force control and commissioning from physical impacts.

comparisons.objective: Release a spring clamp and retrieve a screwdriver into a verified left-hand grasp.
comparisons.physical_skill: Clamp release, coordinated extraction and sustained loaded fingertip grasp.
comparisons.success_condition: Tool freed and held over marker without dropping it or moving the clamp base.
comparisons.reason: Although it involves releasing retention before motion, the tested ability is clamp release and extraction, not adjust-lock sequencing or response-based damper tuning. No separate spec versions were present; the body supplied the rubric.

comparisons.objective: Unplug a USB-C cable and stow a spot welder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize a device, extract a tight plug by its body, then orient and seat the device.
comparisons.success_condition: All four manipulation stages complete; objects safe; arms returned and device still.
comparisons.reason: Same task family as board-TK-GC6557, but still unrelated to tuning and relocking a damping mechanism. No separate spec versions were present; numeric rubric was in the body.

comparisons.objective: Open a stick umbrella until its runner latches, then lift it by the handle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual counterholding and axial pushing against spring force to a latch.
comparisons.success_condition: Runner latched, released and umbrella held up by its handle.
comparisons.reason: Shares bimanual stabilization and a retained state change, but tests axial spring-latch actuation rather than tool-mediated unlock-adjust-lock work and iterative impact response.

comparisons.objective: Post a packet completely through a drop-box flap slot.
comparisons.physical_skill: Packet orientation, insertion, controlled release and possible recontact where the hand cannot follow.
comparisons.success_condition: Packet wholly inside and still, with flap closed.
comparisons.reason: Tests aperture insertion and release planning, not rotary tool engagement, adjustment retention, or dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Intercept a sliding carton and push it into a marked work area.
comparisons.physical_skill: Dynamic interception and nonprehensile planar steering without lifting.
comparisons.success_condition: Carton upright, wholly inside the square and still; falling, tipping or lifting fails.
comparisons.reason: Both involve observing motion, but this task reacts to object translation; it does not infer and tune a mechanism parameter over repeated physical cycles.

comparisons.objective: Draw a measured liquid dose from a vial and return the syringe to its rack.
comparisons.physical_skill: Needle insertion, bimanual syringe stabilization, plunger control and precise restowing.
comparisons.success_condition: 9–11 ml liquid, at most 1 ml air, needle removed, syringe upright and released, arms returned.
comparisons.reason: Tests metered fluid acquisition with simultaneous barrel/plunger control rather than fastener unlocking, collar tuning and impact-response verification.

comparisons.objective: Declutch a powerless valve actuator and close the valve manually.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a declutch lever while turning/regrasping a handwheel until engagement, then continue to a stop.
comparisons.success_condition: Clutch engaged and valve within 5 degrees of closed, held for 3 seconds.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest shared pattern—bimanual stabilization plus rotary state change—but it tests mode engagement and valve closure. The candidate additionally requires recessed hex-key use, a separately locked fine collar, repeated response-based tuning and no-bottoming/rebound validation. No separate spec versions were present; the body supplied the rubric.

comparisons.objective: Empty a robot vacuum dustbin into a waste box and reinstall it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold and orient a bin while pressing a release, control granular discharge, then reseat it.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 9 of 10 particles contained, minimal spill, bin seated with doors shut and arms returned.
comparisons.reason: Tests hold-to-release dumping, containment and reseating, not fine rotary adjustment, tightening torque or repeated dynamic qualification.

comparisons.objective: Intercept two moving slot cars with assigned arms and place them on matching pads.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed bimanual interception, extraction from guides and coordinated placement around a moving distractor.
comparisons.success_condition: Both targets validly extracted while moving and placed; forbidden contact or premature stopping fails.
comparisons.reason: Tests high-speed interception and assignment-specific bimanual coordination, not maintenance-tool manipulation or mechanism tuning. No separate spec versions were present; the body supplied the rubric.

comparisons.objective: Assemble a polarized 2×2 battery pack in a jig.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated tight-clearance cell insertion, polarity control and alignment of two holder halves.
comparisons.success_condition: Bottom holder centered, four cells seated positive-up, top holder centered, assembly still and released.
comparisons.reason: Tests repeated component insertion and orientation in a fixture, with no retained rotary adjustment or closed-loop dynamic-response calibration.

comparisons.objective: Vent the warm cryostat, wait, remove its sample and avoid disturbing the cold unit.
comparisons.physical_skill: State-based selection, timed button actuation, lid removal and careful sample transfer.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct button pressed, three-second wait observed, sample placed in tray; any cold-unit disturbance or premature opening fails.
comparisons.reason: Tests safety reasoning, procedure order and careful extraction, not force-controlled fine adjustment or repeated impact validation. No separate spec versions were present; the body supplied the rubric.

comparisons.objective: Refit and secure a bicycle quick-release front wheel.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual wheel alignment into two dropout slots and over-center lever closure.
comparisons.success_condition: Both axle ends fully seated and lever closed in a safe direction; closing before seating fails.
comparisons.reason: Shares alignment, seating and final locking, but tests assembly retention rather than adjusting a continuous setting from observed dynamic response. No separate spec versions were present; the body supplied the rubric.

comparisons.objective: Load a brush with pollen and hand-pollinate two female flowers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine brush pickup and millimeter-scale contact strokes in the correct sequence.
comparisons.success_condition: Each female receives a qualifying stroke only after pollen is acquired from a male flower.
comparisons.reason: Tests delicate tool-tip trajectories and ordering, not fastener torque, rotary locking or physical cycle commissioning. No separate spec versions were present; the body supplied the rubric.

comparisons.objective: Gently insert a stir bar into a tilted round-bottom flask and restore it to its ring.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual fragile-vessel holding, tilt control and small-object insertion/release.
comparisons.success_condition: Bar inside, flask upright and released in ring; excessive impact, table contact, tipping or bar escape fails.
comparisons.reason: Tests damage-avoiding insertion into fragile glassware, not adjustment of a locked mechanism or repeated dynamic-response convergence. No separate spec versions were present; the body supplied the rubric.

comparisons.objective: Remove a spring peg and clip a hanging photo corner to a wire.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sustained squeeze during transport and thin-object/wire alignment before controlled release.
comparisons.success_condition: Second peg closes on both wire and photo near the corner; photo remains hanging and still.
comparisons.reason: Tests spring-clip transport and thin-layer capture, not tool seating, collar rotation, bounded tightening or commissioning cycles.

comparisons.objective: Snap a scored tile cleanly over a support rod.
comparisons.physical_skill: Symmetric bimanual force application while maintaining score-to-rod registration.
comparisons.success_condition: Clean break; both halves remain on board, released and still; misalignment or unsafe finger placement reduces credit.
comparisons.reason: Tests coordinated bending to fracture a part, not fine reversible adjustment and dynamic performance verification.

comparisons.objective: Unload three bottles from a continuously rocking platform into bins.
comparisons.physical_skill: Motion-timed grasping, transport and upright placement from a periodic moving support.
comparisons.success_condition: All three bottles stand in bins and remain still; knocked-off or uncollected bottles lose credit.
comparisons.reason: Tests interception and placement under periodic disturbance. The candidate instead changes a mechanism setting and evaluates the resulting motion over repeated cycles.

comparisons.objective: Register a block against two perpendicular fixture stops; candidate commissions and locks an adjustable shock absorber through dynamic trials.
comparisons.physical_skill: Block handoff, planar placement and two-face registration versus hex-key engagement, collar adjustment, bounded tightening and response-based iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires ≤1 mm gaps, ≤2° squareness and stable flat placement; candidate requires two safe ≥0.85 J cycles, ≤12 mm travel, no hard-stop strike/rebound/overload and verified lock retention.
comparisons.reason: Both involve precision, but they test different contact mechanics, manipulation sequences and outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Batch-transfer five fragile upright tiles into a box efficiently; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Multi-object grasping and fragile upright transport versus tool insertion, fine rotary adjustment, counterholding and iterative dynamic diagnosis.
comparisons.success_condition: Scores trip count only if every tile remains upright and contained; candidate scores physical unlocking, tuning, relocking and repeatable safe carriage stops.
comparisons.reason: Shared care and bimanual handling are generic; the tested abilities are materially different.

comparisons.objective: Remove a transverse restraint bar and open a drawer; candidate commissions an adjustable damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Recognize obstruction, slide a long bar from sleeves and pull a drawer versus recessed hex-key use, collar rotation, torque control and cyclic tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires bar removal and ≥18 cm drawer opening without damage; candidate requires locked setting retention and two bounded-energy stops without bottoming or rebound.
comparisons.reason: The drawer task tests restraint removal and prismatic opening, not adjustment of dynamic dissipation.

comparisons.objective: Extract a retaining pin while supporting a weighted carriage; candidate adjusts damping on an isolated robot axis.
comparisons.physical_skill: Load support during pin extraction versus setscrew unlocking, fine collar rotation, relocking and repeated impact-response assessment.
comparisons.success_condition: Body reports a full demo and unsafe-event check but provides no complete numeric scoring rubric or spec version; candidate has explicit energy, velocity, stroke and two-cycle thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Even with missing rubric details, load-preserving fastener extraction is clearly different from tuning and validating a damper.

comparisons.objective: Reject an expired analyser kit into pulled-stock storage and call a supervisor; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Semantic safety choice, box placement and button press versus precision tool use, rotary adjustment and force-controlled locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires kit in grey tray plus supervisor call, with zero for inserting it into the analyser; candidate requires safe physical cycles and lock-drift verification.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful overlap beyond generic grasping and control actuation.

comparisons.objective: Arrange five glazed pots in a kiln with specified clearances; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Clearance-constrained multi-object placement and layout planning versus hex-key alignment, collar adjustment, counterholding and dynamic-response iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Body requires upright pots with 2 cm inter-object/post and 1.5 cm wall clearance; no complete spec version or full staged rubric is present. Candidate requires repeatable non-bottoming carriage stops and retained adjustment.
comparisons.reason: The tested ability is collision-free spatial packing, not mechanism commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Pause both working arms during two human stop signals, then resume box loading; candidate adjusts and validates a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Visual interruptibility and coordinated stopping/resumption versus small-tool engagement, fine rotation, tightening and physical cycle diagnosis.
comparisons.success_condition: Zero if combined gripper motion exceeds 3 cm while the paddle is raised; otherwise scores cubes boxed. No complete spec version is present. Candidate uses mechanical safety and performance thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Both concern safety, but one tests behavioral interruption while the other tests physical maintenance and tuning.

comparisons.objective: Unlatch a spot-welder battery lid and tip an 18650 cell into a box; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual hold-and-latch release followed by controlled pouring versus hex-key insertion, fine collar adjustment, relocking and iterative impact testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Body requires lid opened, cell boxed, welder replaced and both arms withdrawn; no complete spec version is present. Candidate requires two repeatable safe stops and witness-tested lock retention.
comparisons.reason: Shared bimanual stabilization is generic; latch release and gravity extraction do not test adjustable damping.

comparisons.objective: Hold a push-fit collet depressed while extracting and laying down a pipe; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sustained axial release force coordinated with pipe pulling versus recessed-tool alignment, collar rotation, bounded tightening and observed-response iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires ≥2.5 mm collet travel, pipe extraction/clearance and stable flat placement without moving the fitting >5 mm; candidate requires safe cyclic stopping and low setting drift.
comparisons.reason: Both manipulate retained mechanisms, but the release-and-extract ability differs materially from calibrated adjustment and verification.

comparisons.objective: Uncap and spike an IV bag, then prime its drip chamber; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a sliding bag, remove cap, align/insert a spike and squeeze a chamber versus hex-key use, collar tuning, locking and dynamic testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires spike lock, one or two valid squeezes, simulated one-third to two-thirds fill and arm withdrawal; candidate requires physical energy dissipation within stroke and rebound limits.
comparisons.reason: Insertion is shared only at a generic level; mechanisms, force sequence and validated outcome are different.

comparisons.objective: Identify, invert and precisely mount a wafer using tweezers, then enable vacuum; candidate adjusts a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Visual discrimination, delicate edge-only tweezer handling, regrasp/inversion and 2 mm placement versus hex-key seating, rotary tuning and torque-controlled locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires correct wafer face-down, centered within 2 mm, flat orientation within 2°, vacuum on and no contamination/drop; candidate requires two safe dynamic stops and retained collar setting.
comparisons.reason: This tests delicate semiconductor identification and mounting, not mechanism response calibration.

comparisons.objective: Tighten a castle nut to the next slot and insert a cotter pin without backing off; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Directionally constrained nut rotation and cross-hole pin insertion versus setscrew unlocking, collar adjustment, relocking and iterative response judgment.
comparisons.success_condition: Body gives staged credit for clockwise alignment and pin insertion, with irreversible zero for >5° backing off; no complete spec version is present. Candidate uses cycle-energy, stroke and drift tests.
comparisons.reason: Some rotary fastener handling overlaps, but the core tested ability—safe cotter-pin alignment—is materially different from damping calibration.

comparisons.objective: Remove a fuel can from a truck, fill it on the ground, then replace it; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Can/nozzle transport and safety-rule sequencing versus precision tool engagement, fine adjustment, locking and impact-response iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Body latches zero if fuel flows while the can is not grounded and clear of the truck; no complete spec version is present. Candidate latches failure on energized adjustment, hard-stop impact or unsafe dynamics.
comparisons.reason: Shared safety sequencing does not make fuel handling and damper commissioning the same tested ability.

comparisons.objective: Raise probes while indexing a wafer stage, then restore contact without scratching; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual sustained probe lift and stage indexing versus tool insertion, collar adjustment, tightening and repeated impact evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Body reports irreversible failure from cumulative lateral probe contact and a full score after safe indexing/return, but omits a complete numeric scoring rubric and spec version. Candidate has explicit energy, velocity, stroke and repeatability criteria.
comparisons.reason: Both use dynamic observation only broadly; probe-clearance coordination is different from damping calibration.

comparisons.objective: Separate a museum jar lid before moving both pieces to a padded tray; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fragile-part separation and sequential transport versus hex-key alignment, fine rotary adjustment, counterholding and torque control.
comparisons.success_condition: Body latches zero if the jar moves with its lid installed or is knocked over; no complete spec version is present. Candidate requires isolated adjustment and repeatable non-bottoming cycles.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful overlap beyond careful bimanual object handling.

comparisons.objective: Crack and open an egg over a bowl, separate contents and dispose of shell halves; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual grasp, impact initiation, shell separation and material sorting versus precision tool insertion, collar rotation, locking and dynamic-response iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires a qualifying rim impact, ≥8 mm shell separation, yolk/white in bowl and shells in tray; candidate requires controlled carriage impacts without hard-stop contact or excessive rebound.
comparisons.reason: Although both include impacts, one tests fracture/opening and sorting while the candidate tests energy-dissipation adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Return a hive frame onto two rests and slide it against neighboring frames; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Long-object lifting, dual-lug seating, leveling and lateral close packing versus hex-key use, fine adjustment, relocking and cyclic diagnosis.
comparisons.success_condition: Body requires both lugs supported, ≤2° level, ≤3° square, ≤5 mm centering and ≤2 mm neighbor gap; no complete spec version is present. Candidate uses dynamic stop and lock-drift thresholds.
comparisons.reason: The hive task is constrained insertion and seating, not adjustable mechanism calibration.

comparisons.objective: Invert and sharply knock a portafilter to eject a puck, then replace it; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Controlled striking with a held container and subsequent reseating versus recessed hex-key engagement, collar adjustment, tightening and iterative cycle assessment.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires puck release inside the knock box while the portafilter remains held, followed by precise replacement; candidate forbids hard-stop impact and instead requires repeatable dissipative stopping.
comparisons.reason: Both involve dynamics, but they test opposite and materially different control: deliberate impulse release versus avoiding impact through damping adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Choose a regulation-compliant joist drilling location and place a guide there; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rule-based spatial selection, guide placement and release versus small-tool manipulation, rotary tuning, locking and dynamic diagnosis.
comparisons.success_condition: Body uses binary compliance with centerline, span-zone and hole-spacing rules; no complete spec version is present. Candidate uses measured physical performance over two cycles.
comparisons.reason: The tested competence is code-constrained placement, not force or mechanism adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Move two museum tankards one at a time, grasping each by its body; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequential fragile-object transport with prohibited grasp regions versus hex-key insertion, counterholding, collar rotation and torque-limited locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Body latches zero for simultaneous lifting or handle/rim lifting; no complete spec version is present. Candidate latches failure for energized adjustment, damage or unsafe cycle dynamics.
comparisons.reason: Shared careful handling and safety constraints are generic; the manipulation mechanisms differ.

comparisons.objective: Support a piano lid while the other arm raises and seats its prop; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual load support and prop insertion under sustained load versus counterholding, recessed-tool use, fine rotary adjustment and iterative response testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Body requires lid raised, prop seated and lid safely resting, with irreversible failure for a fall; no complete spec version is present. Candidate requires two repeatable stops and verified adjustment retention.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual support is shared, but supporting and propping a load is materially different from tuning an energy absorber.

comparisons.objective: Exchange obstructed enclosure modules and close the lid to retain the replacement; candidate adjusts a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Ordered module removal, rail extraction/insertion, replacement seating and enclosure closeout versus hex-key/collar manipulation and response-based commissioning.
comparisons.success_condition: Body states numeric identity, seating, collection, lid, clearance and stability checks with zero for preservation/penetration failures, but supplies no complete thresholds or spec version. Candidate has explicit energy, velocity, stroke, rebound and drift criteria.
comparisons.reason: This is a multi-stage replacement and closeout task, not adjustment of a dynamic mechanism.

comparisons.objective: Use balance feedback and a pipette to correct an under- or overfilled liquid dose to 10.000 g; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Aspiration/dispensing, pressure control and iterative mass correction versus hex-key alignment, collar rotation, tightening and iterative dynamic-response correction.
comparisons.success_condition: Body requires 10.000 ±0.050 g and pipette disposal, with failure if the receiving beaker moves >5 mm; no complete spec version is present. Candidate requires two safe carriage cycles and lock retention.
comparisons.reason: Both iteratively correct based on measurement, but the physical abilities and controlled processes—liquid metering versus impact damping—are meaningfully different.

comparisons.objective: Retrieve a block from a cyclic machine hazard zone only during the parked phase; candidate tunes an isolated damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Time entry and withdrawal around a moving bar plus pick-and-place versus precision maintenance tooling, rotary adjustment and guarded test cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Immediate zero if robot or block comes within 2 cm of the bar; full score requires stable tray placement. Candidate requires de-energized adjustment followed by controlled cycles without bottoming, rebound or hard-stop contact.
comparisons.reason: Both involve moving-machine safety, but temporal hazard avoidance is different from physical damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Run a fair experiment to identify the higher-friction sled and place it on a mat; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Equalize mass, operate launchers, compare travel and classify a sled versus hex-key insertion, collar tuning, torque-controlled locking and interpreting stop dynamics.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires both sleds launched at equal total mass, neither hitting the end wall, correct friction inference and selection; candidate requires prescribed impact energy/velocity and two repeatable safe stops after physical relocking.
comparisons.reason: Both use repeated dynamics and observed motion, but one tests experimental control and material inference while the candidate tests mechanical adjustment and retention.

comparisons.objective: Clear only the cartons obstructing a photo-eye beam; unlike commissioning a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Selective carton displacement and spatial line-of-sight reasoning, not tool engagement, collar adjustment, locking, or impact-response tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Beam clear; two blockers moved no more than 10 cm; other cartons untouched and upright. Complete numeric rubric available.
comparisons.reason: Tests minimal scene intervention, not adjustment and verification of a retained damping mechanism.

comparisons.objective: Orient an 18650 cell into a spot welder and latch its lid; unrelated to damper commissioning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cell extraction, reorientation, close-fit placement, welder stabilization, and lid latching. It shares bimanual stabilization only as a generic primitive.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct-polarity cell seated, lid caught, welder reoriented and released safely. The body supplies the rubric; no separate spec version is present.
comparisons.reason: Tests polarity-aware insertion and latching, not iterative mechanical tuning or post-adjustment dynamic behavior.

comparisons.objective: Position two masking plates to expose only a coating band, not adjust machinery.
comparisons.physical_skill: Planar pick-place and precise coverage alignment; no threaded tool use, locking, force-limited tightening, or dynamic diagnosis.
comparisons.success_condition: Both grey zones covered while the orange band remains exposed, under version-specific 2–5 mm or percentage tolerances.
comparisons.reason: The measured ability is spatial masking accuracy, meaningfully different from tuning and retaining a damper.

comparisons.objective: Hold a sprung picture-frame back flush while turning four retaining clips.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual preload maintenance, clip rotation, and hand swapping. Rotation and retention overlap only at a generic level; there is no tool insertion or response tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Four clips rotated at least 80 degrees, back flush within 3 mm/1.5 degrees, hands released, arms returned.
comparisons.reason: Tests maintaining spring preload while sequentially closing clips, not selecting a damping setting through repeated impacts.

comparisons.objective: Extract a stuck pin by repeatedly impacting a slide hammer, then rack the tool.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hook insertion, shaft alignment, bimanual stabilization, and momentum-generating blows; no fine adjustment or locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Available body says repeated above-threshold impacts must extract the pin and steady pulls must fail, but the full numeric scoring rubric is absent.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve dynamic mechanics and bimanual tool control, this tests impact-tool momentum for extraction rather than tuning a damper from observed response.

comparisons.objective: Glue and hold a broken mug handle in alignment until the bond sets.
comparisons.physical_skill: Nozzle placement, two-point alignment, stabilization, and timed holding; no threaded adjustment or locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Glue on both patches; handle held within 6 mm/10 degrees on a still mug for 3 seconds; safe released final state.
comparisons.reason: Tests adhesive application and mating-part alignment, not adjustable-component commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Orient and place a pressure-relief cushion correctly in a wheelchair.
comparisons.physical_skill: Large-object reorientation, regrasping, and controlled lowering between guards; no tools, locking, or force-response adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct orientation and stable seat placement within stated pose tolerances. The body reports numeric criteria but no separate spec version.
comparisons.reason: Tests semantic orientation and placement, not mechanical calibration.

comparisons.objective: Apply an opaque primer coat while controlling brush loading and drips.
comparisons.physical_skill: Brush handling, wiping, repeated dipping, contact strokes, and coverage control; no fine rotary adjuster or retention fastener.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 95% opaque coverage, at most one drip, no off-target brushing, brush safely released; versions differ in fluid/bristle fidelity.
comparisons.reason: Tests process-material application and spill avoidance rather than tuning machinery.

comparisons.objective: Fit a long wardrobe rail into closed and open supports using a tilt-in sequence.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual long-part handling, end insertion, coordinated swing-down, and release; no adjustment or locking torque.
comparisons.success_condition: Left end inserted at least 0.8 cm, right end on its support, rail level within 1 degree and released still.
comparisons.reason: Tests constrained long-part insertion, not adjustment followed by operational verification.

comparisons.objective: Connect booster clamps in a safe electrical order.
comparisons.physical_skill: Spring-clamp opening and seating plus cable management; generic force control and alignment do not establish duplication.
comparisons.success_condition: Four self-held connections in the required order; unsafe polarity, ordering, or jaw contact forces zero.
comparisons.reason: Tests ordered safety-critical clamp placement, not tuning and locking an adjustable mechanism.

comparisons.objective: Operate a spring-return coffee shelf, fill a mug, and return it safely to its saucer.
comparisons.physical_skill: Shelf holding, vessel handling, control actuation, and spill avoidance; not adjuster manipulation or threaded locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Body reports 120 ml retained, zero spill, no hot-stream/wall contact, and safe final placement, but omits the complete tiered numeric scorer.
comparisons.reason: Tests coordinated beverage service under spill and thermal constraints, not machinery commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Measure and cut a DIN rail to a specified length using a bench cutter.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rail feeding, scale alignment, bimanual holding, and lever actuation. It does not require iterative tuning or a retained setting.
comparisons.success_condition: First stroke must cut at 250 mm within 1 mm while rail motion remains below 0.5 mm; simulated cutting fidelity is explicitly limited.
comparisons.reason: Tests measurement-to-length and stabilization during cutting, not dynamic-response calibration.

comparisons.objective: Load a vial into a vacuum desiccator, evacuate it, isolate it, and stop the pump.
comparisons.physical_skill: Dome removal/reseating, vial placement, stopcock rotation, switch operation, and pressure monitoring.
comparisons.success_condition: Vial upright on the ring, dome sealed, pressure at or below -90 kPa, stopcock shut, pump off, with venting no faster than 12 kPa/s.
comparisons.reason: Tests vacuum-process sequencing and seal management, not adjustable damping.

comparisons.objective: Peel protective film while holding an acrylic sheet down and discard the film.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual counterholding, tab pinch, controlled peeling trajectory, and deformable-proxy handling; no rotary adjustment or lock.
comparisons.success_condition: All four strips peeled into the basket without tab tear or excessive sheet translation/tilt.
comparisons.reason: Counterholding is shared generically, but the tested ability is peel-force management across a breakable bond.

comparisons.objective: Route a condensate hose with continuous downhill fall into a drain.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual flexible-object routing over supports and nozzle placement; no tools, adjustment setting, or locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Nozzle in tundish, hose supported on both steps, released, and cumulative rise no more than 5 mm for full credit.
comparisons.reason: Tests global shape control of a flexible hose, not rigid mechanism tuning.

comparisons.objective: Identify hidden cable endpoints and place only the correct plugs into holders.
comparisons.physical_skill: Interactive cable tracing, careful tugging, cable handling, and plug placement; no mechanical adjustment or force-limited fastener work.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct red and blue plugs released in matching holders while three distractor plugs stay within 5 cm and no cable pulls out.
comparisons.reason: Tests identity inference through cable motion and selective placement.

comparisons.objective: Determine a gauge's zero error and level a platform with motorized foot buttons.
comparisons.physical_skill: Instrument placement, reversal/reference calibration, button actuation, and iterative measurement-based correction. This overlaps in closed-loop adjustment but not in the physical interface or dynamic phenomenon.
comparisons.success_condition: Gauge characterized against the reference or reversal test, then true platform tilt within 0.15 degrees.
comparisons.reason: Tests metrology and bias compensation; the candidate tests damping-response tuning plus physical unlock/relock and witness-torque retention.

comparisons.objective: Retrieve diagonal cutters from a crowded pegboard and place them on a mat.
comparisons.physical_skill: Clutter-aware grasping and lift-then-pull hook clearance; no adjuster, fastener, or dynamic testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Cutters stable over the mat with no other tool fallen; dropping any tool off the table fails.
comparisons.reason: Tests safe tool retrieval from an upturned peg.

comparisons.objective: Unscrew a flashlight cap, pour out its battery, and set the parts down safely.

comparisons.success_condition: Repeated safe stopping behavior with a locked setting versus the correct model built without jamming the conveyor or accepting look-alikes.
