comparisons.objective: Tune and lock a shock absorber versus hold a spring-loaded cage door shut while throwing its slide bolt.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key use, collar tuning, and torque-limited retention versus simultaneous door bracing and linear bolt sliding.
comparisons.success_condition: Two repeatable non-bottoming cycles and no setting drift versus a shut, bolted, stationary door with both grippers clear.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual stabilization is shared, but dynamic parameter commissioning is not equivalent to maintaining closure while latching.

comparisons.objective: Tune damping for safe repeatable impacts versus raise and rotate a monitor, then re-engage its spring axis locks.
comparisons.physical_skill: Recessed-tool engagement, collar rotation, counterholding, and bounded setscrew torque versus supporting a large articulated load while translating, pivoting, and relocking axes.
comparisons.success_condition: Measured stopping performance and witness-tested setting retention versus prescribed screen height/orientation, preserved tilt, relocking, and 20 seconds hands-off.
comparisons.reason: Unlock-adjust-relock is shared, but the candidate tests performance-driven damping iteration under impacts rather than static pose reconfiguration. The record body omits exact pose tolerances, yet its tested ability is sufficiently clear.

comparisons.objective: Commission a damper versus close and seal a swing-top bottle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool-mediated unlock, fine tuning, and relock versus positioning a stopper and driving an over-center lever while bracing a bottle.
comparisons.success_condition: Two safe stops with retained adjustment versus stopper seated and lever held past center without tipping.
comparisons.reason: Both include bimanual bracing and retention, but over-center closure is mechanically and behaviorally different from iterative dynamic tuning. All three spec versions support this distinction.

comparisons.objective: Commission a shock absorber versus identify and isolate the leaking coolant branch.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key alignment and fine locked adjustment versus visual pipe tracing and quarter-turn valve manipulation.
comparisons.success_condition: Safe repeatable carriage deceleration versus only the spraying branch shut and the other two left open.
comparisons.reason: The coolant task emphasizes routing inference and selective isolation, not tuning or retained dynamic performance.

comparisons.objective: Tune and lock a damper versus remove a slip-sheet without displacing its load.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine tool use and adjustment under torque constraints versus coordinated pulling and load bracing against friction.
comparisons.success_condition: Two non-bottoming stops and no setting drift versus sheet fully removed while block motion and tilt remain below limits.
comparisons.reason: Generic counterholding is shared, but the controlled interaction and measured outcome are different.

comparisons.objective: Commission a rigid-body damper versus attach a cable to fish tape and pull it through conduit.
comparisons.physical_skill: Recessed hex-key insertion and collar locking versus deformable hook-and-eye engagement and hand-over-hand pulling.
comparisons.success_condition: Repeated safe impact absorption with retained setting versus the hooked eyelet and cable emerging from the far conduit mouth by at least 5 cm.
comparisons.reason: The cable task tests deformable routing and hook retention, not mechanism tuning or impact response.

comparisons.objective: Tune and lock a shock absorber versus rotate manifold fittings to establish a leak-free coolant path.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool-mediated fine adjustment and torque-controlled locking versus planning and turning several indexed rotary fittings.
comparisons.success_condition: Two safe stopping cycles with no drift versus coolant connectivity to the outlet with no open branch and hands clear.
comparisons.reason: Rotation is a shared generic primitive only; network-routing configuration is meaningfully different from dynamic damping commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Commission and lock a damper versus push a separate assembly spacer through a covered path and recover it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key insertion, collar tuning, counterholding, and locking versus pusher placement, constrained displacement, recovery, and tool parking.
comparisons.success_condition: Two repeatable safe stops and retained adjustment versus spacer extracted and both spacer and pusher released in their required states.
comparisons.reason: Tool use is shared, but extraction through a constrained path does not test parameter tuning or dynamic energy absorption. The record omits its numeric scoring rubric and detailed path geometry, though the objective remains clearly distinct.

comparisons.objective: Commission a damper versus extract a retaining pin while supporting a weighted carriage.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine setscrew/collar manipulation and dynamic testing versus load support coordinated with pin extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: No bottoming, overload, rebound, or drift across two cycles versus pin removed without carriage height loss or dropping the load.
comparisons.reason: Both concern machinery and carriage safety, but one tunes energy absorption while the other transfers support during fastener removal. Exact height and violation thresholds are missing from the record.

comparisons.objective: Tune and lock a robot-axis damper versus connect a flexible sensor cable to a ZIF connector.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key alignment, collar rotation, and torque-limited locking versus latch opening, flexible-strip insertion, maintaining seating, and latch closure.
comparisons.success_condition: Repeated safe impacts with a retained setting versus cable fully seated and latched after the required operation order.
comparisons.reason: Although both require fine bimanual manipulation and ordered locking, flexible insertion into a ZIF connector is a meaningfully different tested ability. Numeric seating and latch thresholds are absent from the record.

comparisons.objective: Commission a shock absorber versus shuffle a sorted deck under a color constraint and deal it in turn.
comparisons.physical_skill: Precision tool engagement and mechanism tuning versus repeated thin-tile regrasping, restacking, and sequential placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Two safe, repeatable stops with lock retention versus a valid mixed deck followed by six correct clockwise deals without drops.
comparisons.reason: The objectives and physical skills are unrelated. The body supplies scoring increments but omits detailed pose tolerances.

comparisons.objective: Commission and lock a damper versus test a toilet flush lever and file the matching condition report.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key/collar adjustment followed by physical impact trials versus pressing or inspecting a rocker and placing a diagnostic tag.
comparisons.success_condition: Measured safe stopping performance over two cycles versus correct classification of working, stiff, or missing lever.
comparisons.reason: Both involve physical testing, but the toilet task diagnoses a discrete state rather than adjusting and validating a mechanism. Lever thresholds and tag-pad tolerance details are only partly specified.

comparisons.objective: Commission and lock a damper versus test a toilet flush lever and file the matching condition report.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key/collar adjustment followed by physical impact trials versus pressing or inspecting a rocker and placing a diagnostic tag.
comparisons.success_condition: Measured safe stopping performance over two cycles versus correct classification of working, stiff, or missing lever.
comparisons.reason: This record duplicates pr-1254, but remains distinct from the candidate: diagnosis and reporting do not test iterative damping adjustment. Some lever thresholds are absent.

comparisons.objective: Commission a damper versus pack food and scented toiletries into a bear canister and lock its lid.
comparisons.physical_skill: Recessed tool engagement and precise collar locking versus multi-object packing, lid placement, and quarter-turn closure.
comparisons.success_condition: Two safe impact cycles and retained setting versus all four required items enclosed before the canister is locked.
comparisons.reason: Shared closure/rotation primitives do not make the tasks equivalent; packing under an implicit inclusion rule tests different planning and manipulation. Exact containment tolerances are not supplied.

comparisons.objective: Tune a shock absorber versus cook and serve two patties safely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine tool alignment, adjustment, and locking versus coordinated two-spatula scooping, bracing, flipping, and timed handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Repeatable non-bottoming stops without overload or drift versus both patty sides cooked for 20–40 seconds and served without contamination, burns, drops, or forbidden contact.
comparisons.reason: The tasks differ across objective, physical control, temporal reasoning, and safety failures.

comparisons.objective: Commission and lock a damper versus reseat a loose AED pad, clear the patient, and press SHOCK.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key/collar manipulation and repeated guarded cycling versus compliant pad pressing, withdrawing both arms, and button actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Two safe mechanical stopping cycles with retained adjustment versus pad seated and no gripper within 15 cm during the shock interval.
comparisons.reason: Generic pressing and safety sequencing are insufficient for overlap; the candidate tests mechanical tuning and lock retention.

comparisons.objective: Commission a shock absorber versus lift and carry a chest onto a rug without dragging it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Small-interface tool use, fine adjustment, and torque control versus symmetric bimanual grasping, load lifting, transport, and placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Two repeatable safe stops with no drift versus chest placed on the rug with less than 2 cm accumulated floor sliding.
comparisons.reason: The manipulation scales, contacts, and measured outcomes are plainly different. Exact rug-placement tolerances are not given in the record body.

comparisons.objective: Tune and lock a robot-axis damper versus load and secure a bicycle on a bus rack.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key insertion, collar adjustment, and witness-tested locking versus large articulated-object lifting, channel alignment, support-arm deployment, and release.
comparisons.success_condition: Safe repeated carriage deceleration versus bike secured in the outer rack position, upright, released, and stationary.
comparisons.reason: Both involve equipment safety, but the actual tested abilities and success states are unrelated. The record provides its key tilt and stability limits.

comparisons.objective: Commission a damper versus denest two rigid trays and park them in separate bays.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine tool alignment, collar tuning, and torque-limited locking versus tab grasping, clearance lifting, lateral transport, and precise placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Two non-bottoming stops with retained setting versus both trays released, upright, stable, separated, and within bay pose tolerances.
comparisons.reason: Rigid-body manipulation is the only broad commonality; denesting and parking do not test adjustment, locking, or dynamic response.

comparisons.objective: Sequential gold lift-off/rinsing with drip and waste control; candidate commissions a shock absorber by iterative adjustment.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cassette transfer among baths and controlled dish pouring, not hex-key engagement, collar rotation, locking, or dynamic tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct bath order/times, continuous wetness, caught/disposed drips, and no contamination; no impact-response or lock-drift test.
comparisons.reason: Different process, mechanism, manipulation, and measured outcome.

comparisons.objective: Inspect hidden carton labels and dispense the 10 mg pack; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Reorienting look-alike cartons for visual inspection and selection, not tool insertion, retained-collar adjustment, or force-limited locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Red-band carton checked and placed in basket with no wrong-strength carton; no dynamic cycles or retention test.
comparisons.reason: Tests active visual inspection and selection rather than mechanical commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Interlock three slotted boards into a partition; candidate adjusts a damper to produce safe repeatable stops.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual board stabilization, slot alignment, and downward insertion versus recessed hex-key use, fine collar rotation, and tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Two crossings interlocked within pose tolerances and aligned to a mark; no response tuning or witness-torque requirement.
comparisons.reason: Shared bimanual stabilization is generic; the tested assemblies and abilities differ materially.

comparisons.objective: Open a threaded flashlight, remove its battery, and sort the parts; candidate commissions an adjustable shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Counterholding plus repeated cap twist/regrasp, axial thread following, tipping, and placement. It lacks key insertion, retained adjustment, locking torque, and response-based iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Cap and battery removed and deposited safely, flashlight replaced; body supplies numeric stages but no separate spec version.
comparisons.reason: Some rotational regrasp overlap is generic; threaded disassembly and battery extraction do not test damper adjustment or dynamic validation.

comparisons.objective: Partition weighted parcels between two totes without exceeding either limit; candidate tunes a mechanical damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Parcel carrying, cross-workspace transfer, and weight-based allocation, not fine tool use or force-controlled adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Five parcels split so both totes remain at or below 7 kg; indexed record has no spec version or complete numeric pose rubric.
comparisons.reason: The decision problem and manipulation outcome are unrelated; missing pose details do not suggest duplication.

comparisons.objective: Singulate four parcels onto a sorter lane with spacing and orientation; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Carton extraction, staging handoffs, and planar placement, not fastener access, collar tuning, or locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Single-file, flat, aligned parcels with at least 10 cm gaps and no stacking; indexed record has no spec version/full scoring rubric.
comparisons.reason: Tests parcel singulation rather than mechanical adjustment and impact-response control.

comparisons.objective: Keep a station stocked in time for another robot's fixed cycle; candidate iteratively tunes carriage stopping behavior.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed cube pick/place around a moving collaborator, not hex-key alignment, fine rotation, tightening, or diagnostic adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: All six blocks crated, with zero for arm contact; all three spec versions agree.
comparisons.reason: Both involve repeated cycles, but one tests production pacing and collision avoidance, not parameter tuning from physical response.

comparisons.objective: Unload blocks from a motor-driven carousel before they return to the loading arm; candidate adjusts a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Time-critical interception and bin placement around moving equipment, not tool-mediated loosening, adjustment, and relocking.
comparisons.success_condition: All five cubes crated with no inter-arm contact; all three spec versions agree.
comparisons.reason: Shared interaction with cyclic machinery is contextual; the tested physical ability is different.

comparisons.objective: Arrange cartons into stable stacks satisfying a height-to-base rule; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Box orientation, stacking, and bimanual handoff versus small-tool engagement and fine force-controlled adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: All cartons correctly stacked with no stack exceeding three times its base; no complete indexed spec or full geometric rubric.
comparisons.reason: Tests stability-aware packing, not commissioning or dynamic response.

comparisons.objective: Compute and place exactly 70p change; candidate commissions a robot-axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coin selection and placement, using oversized rigid tokens, not mechanical adjustment or locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Dish total exactly 70p; overpayment partial and underpayment zero.
comparisons.reason: Arithmetic selection and token handling are unrelated to the candidate's mechanism and validation.

comparisons.objective: Install a chest tip restraint before loading and closing its drawer; candidate tunes a shock absorber while isolated.
comparisons.physical_skill: Slide a bolt into a catch, then load and close a drawer; no hex-key turning, fine retained-collar adjustment, or iterative response diagnosis.
comparisons.success_condition: Restraint fitted before loading so the chest does not tip; indexed record lacks a complete numeric scoring spec.
comparisons.reason: Both encode safe sequencing around equipment, but the physical mechanism and tested outcome differ materially.

comparisons.objective: Repair a pipe gap using correctly sized slip couplings; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Size discrimination, coaxial pipe insertion, coupling staging, and axial sliding versus recessed-key use, collar rotation, and torque locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Replacement captured and both correct couplings closed over joints, with release/stillness and no dropped parts; no indexed spec version with full thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Mechanical assembly is shared only broadly; the repair does not test adjustment from dynamic response.

comparisons.objective: Fill a bath while enforcing cold-first and hot-off-first sequencing; candidate tunes an isolated damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Quarter-turn tap operation with coordinated arms, not tool alignment, fastener loosening, collar tuning, or lock verification.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct tap sequence and computed fill level; hot running alone causes sticky zero. No indexed spec version and water is not physically simulated.
comparisons.reason: Tests safety ordering of controls rather than force-controlled mechanical commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Seat a blind headrail in two gated brackets and close both retainers; candidate adjusts and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual long-part transport, two-end alignment, insertion, and gate latching versus small-tool access and fine rotational tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Rail home within floor/back/tilt/depth tolerances and both gates shut; both spec versions agree.
comparisons.reason: A meaningfully different insertion-and-latching ability; generic alignment and bimanual handling do not establish overlap.

comparisons.objective: Close a hand nutcracker, then sort kernel and shell pieces; candidate calibrates a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Symmetric bimanual handle compression and small-part sorting, not keyed loosening, controlled collar rotation, relocking, or iterative dynamic adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Jaw closure triggers a simulated rigid-body swap, then kernel/shell placement and arm return; both specs agree.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve force, the nutcracker tests opposing compression, not parameter adjustment or retention under repeated impacts.

comparisons.objective: Identify water versus acetone and put only water on a hotplate; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Safe beaker selection, transport, and upright placement, not tool use or mechanical tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Water upright on plate; zero for acetone proximity, tipping, or loss. No separate indexed spec version.
comparisons.reason: Tests hazard inference and liquid-container handling, not adjustment and dynamic validation.

comparisons.objective: Choose and place the correctly sized blood-pressure cuff on a training arm; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Width-based selection and pose-controlled cuff placement; rigid cuff handling does not include keyed access, fine collar adjustment, or tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: 8 cm cuff centered and oriented above elbow with no other cuff present; no indexed spec version beyond body rubric.
comparisons.reason: Different selection and placement ability with unrelated completion criteria.

comparisons.objective: Clear loose cups while detecting and leaving one force-retained cup; candidate adjusts a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Gentle probing to distinguish breakaway resistance, then cup transport; candidate instead counterholds, loosens, rotates, tightens, and evaluates impacts.
comparisons.success_condition: Both loose cups upright in tray; zero if stuck cup moves over 3 mm, tips, or falls. No indexed spec version.
comparisons.reason: Both require force sensitivity, but one tests nondestructive property probing while the other tests tunable mechanism commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Restock two amenity trays to exact par and leave surplus on the cart; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Inventory-aware item placement and midline handoff, not fine tool manipulation or iterative force-response adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Each tray has exactly one soap and one upright shampoo, with spare retained; indexed record lacks a complete numeric spec.
comparisons.reason: Tests exact-count restocking rather than mechanical adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Store raw chicken below ready-to-eat salad; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Two-arm container placement onto rack tiers, not fastener/collar manipulation or response-guided tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Chicken on lower tier and salad above, with zero for hazardous high placement/overlap; no indexed spec version with full thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Tests food-safety ordering and placement, not the candidate's mechanical ability.

comparisons.objective: Return all remaining surgical instruments from a drape to a tray; candidate adjusts and validates a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Instrument pickup, transfer, and count completion versus hex-key insertion, counterholding, fine rotation, and torque-limited locking.
comparisons.success_condition: All four instruments on tray and drape clear; indexed body omits the numeric scoring table and has no spec version.
comparisons.reason: The objective and manipulation are unrelated; absent scoring details do not create a plausible duplicate.

comparisons.objective: Correct 2+3 by removing one of six blocks to a spare tray; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Simple block pickup and placement guided by arithmetic, not tool engagement or force-controlled mechanism adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Exactly five blocks remain on mat and the sixth is in the spare tray.
comparisons.reason: Tests arithmetic correction through pick-and-place, not commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Run a press using continuous two-hand controls, then remove the finished part; candidate tunes an isolated damper and cycles it from a guarded control.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sustained simultaneous button holding and post-cycle retrieval versus hex-key engagement, collar adjustment, relocking, and diagnostic iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Both controls held throughout closing stroke before part removal; body lacks numeric timing/pose thresholds and no spec version is indexed.
comparisons.reason: Physical control actuation is shared, but it is central two-hand safeguarding here and only one step in the candidate; the principal tested abilities differ.

comparisons.objective: Sort rigid cloth representations into area-coded buckets; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Color/category selection and block-like placement, not actual deformable cloth handling or fine mechanical adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Red in toilet bucket and green in kitchen bucket, with hazardous cross-contamination penalized.
comparisons.reason: Different semantic sorting objective and manipulation; color/layout changes are not being used as the novelty basis.

comparisons.objective: Open the clean-ice source and use a scoop to serve uncontaminated ice; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Lid manipulation, scoop use, source selection, and contamination avoidance versus keyed adjustment, counterholding, tightening, and repeated impact assessment.
comparisons.success_condition: At least one clean cube delivered by scoop after lid opening with no contamination; body lacks the complete numeric scorer and no spec version is indexed.
comparisons.reason: Tests hygienic tool-mediated transfer, not mechanical commissioning or dynamic stopping performance.

comparisons.objective: Serve clean ice from the correct source; candidate commissions and locks an industrial-axis damper through repeated impact trials.
comparisons.physical_skill: Scoop handling and contamination avoidance versus recessed hex-key engagement, collar tuning, counterholding, and torque-limited locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Clean cube delivered without contamination versus two repeatable ≥0.85 J stops within 12 mm, without bottoming, rebound, overload, or drift. Ice record omits detailed numeric manipulation tolerances.
comparisons.reason: Different objective and tested ability; generic grasping does not establish overlap.

comparisons.objective: Chock a rolling cradle before unloading it; candidate tunes and locks a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Place two chocks and perform a restrained lift versus tool insertion, fine collar rotation, bimanual counterhold, and iterative response-based adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Both chocks remain seated while the load moves versus two safe, repeatable dynamic stops and retained collar setting. Chock record gives no seating tolerances.
comparisons.reason: Static stabilization-before-removal does not test damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Seat a keyed coupling and prove rotary drive transfer; candidate adjusts damping and proves stopping performance.
comparisons.physical_skill: Keyed alignment, insertion, and rotational engagement versus hex-key unlocking, collar tuning, relocking, and guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Continuous coupling engagement with lower-rotor motion and no direct drive versus bounded stroke, impact energy/velocity, rebound, overload, and drift over two cycles. Coupling record lacks numeric seating/transfer thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Both verify a mechanism after manipulation, but the core insertion/drive-transfer ability differs from iterative dynamic tuning.

comparisons.objective: Extend a training handle and engage its detent; candidate commissions a damper setting.
comparisons.physical_skill: Withdraw pin, translate telescoping member, and re-engage detent versus recessed tool use, fine rotary adjustment, counterholding, and torque-controlled set-screw locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Measured extension with pin kept clear then positively engaged versus two dynamically acceptable stops and witness-tested setting retention. Handle record omits extension and engagement thresholds.
comparisons.reason: A latch-and-translate sequence does not test response-guided damping adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Support a bar before withdrawing its carriage; candidate tunes an axis shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual load support and relative carriage withdrawal versus tool alignment, collar rotation, locking, and iterative impact inspection.
comparisons.success_condition: Alternate support continuously carries the bar and carriage gains real clearance versus two safe stops within the damper envelope. Bar record lacks numeric clearance/support thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Load transfer and withdrawal are meaningfully different from damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Balance a radiator valve by closing it while counting turns and reopening halfway; candidate finds and locks a damping setting from observed motion.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sustained wheel rotation with hidden-state turn counting versus hex-key engagement, counterholding, fine collar adjustment, locking, and repeated physical trials.
comparisons.success_condition: Final opening equals half the counted initial turns versus two consecutive non-bottoming, low-rebound stops with setting retention. Valve record does not state angular/count tolerance.
comparisons.reason: Both rotate an adjuster, but one tests motion counting and arithmetic while the other tests tool-mediated locking and feedback-based dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Track an unpredictably moving figure with a camera and react to a lamp; candidate commissions a mechanical damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuous long-bar tracking plus cross-arm cue response versus fine tool insertion, rotary adjustment, counterholding, and bounded tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Keep target framed and press a remote button within 1 s versus two acceptable physical carriage stops and no setting drift. Framing tolerance is missing.
comparisons.reason: Visuomotor tracking and cue response are unrelated to damper adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Hands-free pipette-tip replacement and re-docking; candidate adjusts and locks a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Passive-sleeve ejection, compliant tip seating, and docking versus recessed hex-key use, collar tuning, counterhold, and locking torque.
comparisons.success_condition: Dispose used tip, retain fresh tip, avoid all tip contact/drop/tip-over, and dock versus two safe dynamic stops with no drift. Tip record lacks seating-force and alignment thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Different objective and contact mechanics; generic alignment and force control alone do not make them duplicates.

comparisons.objective: Rearrange household items by use frequency for accessible storage; candidate commissions robot-axis damping.
comparisons.physical_skill: Multi-object pick-and-place and shelf planning versus fine tool manipulation and feedback-driven mechanism adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Specified items rest on assigned shelves within 8 mm and 15° versus impact-energy, stroke, rebound, overload, and lock-retention criteria.
comparisons.reason: Accessibility-oriented placement does not test mechanical commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Insert a loose-cord barrel plug into a held jack and lay the assembly down; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual connector alignment and insertion versus recessed tool engagement, counterheld collar rotation, and torque-limited locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Connector fully seated within 0.5 mm/5° and 1 mm mouth gap, then released and arms returned versus two acceptable impact stops and retained setting.
comparisons.reason: Connector insertion is a different tested ability and is expressly outside the candidate family.

comparisons.objective: Choose protective packaging, close it, and validate the packed sensor by a drop test; candidate commissions an adjustable axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pack, cushion, tuck lid, and release for a drop versus hex-key unlocking, fine collar adjustment, counterhold, relocking, and iterative cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Sensor remains below 50 g and stable after a 30 cm drop versus carriage absorbs ≥0.85 J within 12 mm without hard-stop contact, rebound, overload, or drift.
comparisons.reason: Both assess shock response, but packaging selection/closure and damper tuning are meaningfully different objectives and manipulation abilities.

comparisons.objective: Start a hex nut without cross-threading using back-turn-and-drop; candidate adjusts and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coaxial nut placement, thread feel, reverse rotation, and hand running versus recessed hex-key seating, collar tuning, counterholding, and set-screw torque control.
comparisons.success_condition: Body provides no rubric details beyond the trained thread-start procedure; candidate requires two quantified safe cycles and retention testing.
comparisons.reason: Thread-starting is different from adjustment and dynamic validation; missing nut thresholds do not create plausible duplication.

comparisons.objective: Lift and place a rabbit while continuously supporting its back; candidate commissions an industrial damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinated whole-body bimanual support and transport versus fine tool use, rotary adjustment, counterhold, and guarded machine cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: No spine bend over 25° or fall of 3 cm, then place in carrier versus two repeatable safe stops with no setting drift.
comparisons.reason: Animal-support manipulation is unrelated to damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Clean a wafer by holding it with pliers while sweeping a blow gun; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool-mediated wafer holding and coordinated sweeping versus hex-key insertion, collar rotation, counterholding, locking, and iterative response inspection.
comparisons.success_condition: Remove 12 surrogate particles and return wafer and gun to supports versus quantified energy, velocity, stroke, rebound, overload, and drift limits. Cleaning record omits sweep and placement tolerances.
comparisons.reason: Different tools, objective, and measured outcome; shared bimanual tool use is generic.

comparisons.objective: Clean a chip through solvent baths while avoiding a hazardous solvent-wet piranha transfer; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequential dipping, timed submersion, and hazard-aware handling versus fine mechanical adjustment, locking, and repeated guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Two-second ordered baths and safe holder placement, with zero for unsafe piranha transfer, versus two safe carriage stops and retention testing.
comparisons.reason: Chemical sequence and hazard recognition do not test damper tuning.

comparisons.objective: Place an already-unscrewed reagent cap inside-up without contaminating its interior; candidate adjusts and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Delicate cap reorientation and forbidden-contact avoidance versus recessed tool insertion, counterholding, collar tuning, and bounded tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Release cap on rest with no interior/rim contact versus two quantified acceptable stops and post-lock drift tolerance. Cap record omits pose/contact-clearance thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Protected-surface handling is a different tested ability.

comparisons.objective: Remove a loose hex key obstructing a cabinet track and open the guided door; candidate uses a hex key to commission a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Obstacle extraction and prismatic door motion versus inserting that tool into a recessed screw, unlocking, fine adjustment, relocking, and cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Door opens 288.23 mm while key stays in the work area and guide remains valid versus two safe, repeatable stops and lock retention.

comparisons.objective: Read an analog clock and set a digital bedside clock, versus tune a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Visual time interpretation and counted button presses versus precision hex-tool work, collar control, and physical cycle evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Digital time reaches 4:39–4:41, with partial credit for correct minutes, versus two mechanically safe stops and a stable locked adjustment.
comparisons.reason: Only generic control actuation is shared. No spec versions are present; button travel and actuation-force thresholds are omitted.

comparisons.objective: Hang IV and drainage bags at medically correct relative heights, versus commission a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bag identification, transport, hook alignment, and hanging versus fastener manipulation, fine rotary tuning, and repeated impact testing.
comparisons.success_condition: IV bag above the patient and drainage bag below the bladder versus two safe carriage stops with no bottoming or setting drift.
comparisons.reason: The manipulation and judged physical relationship are unrelated. No spec versions are present; exact height bands, hook engagement, and release criteria are missing from the body.

comparisons.objective: Insert multimeter leads into the correct jacks, versus adjust and lock a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sub-millimetre banana-pin alignment and insertion with semantic jack selection versus hex-key insertion, counterholding, collar tuning, and force-limited locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Black lead in COM and red lead in V/ohm, not 10 A, versus two safe damped cycles and post-lock retention.
comparisons.reason: Both require precise insertion, but the candidate's tested ability is adjustment, torque retention, and dynamic commissioning rather than connector placement. No spec versions are present; insertion depth and retention-force thresholds are omitted.

comparisons.objective: Adjust a rheostat until a bulb reaches rated voltage, versus adjust a damper until a carriage stops safely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize a free rheostat and slide its passive contact from meter feedback versus unlock a collar with a hex key, rotate it finely, relock it, and evaluate impacts.
comparisons.success_condition: Hold 4.8–5.2 V for one second without exceeding 7 V versus two safe cycles within energy, velocity, stroke, rebound, overload, and drift constraints.
comparisons.reason: Both test feedback-guided adjustment, but electrical set-point control without a lock or impact dynamics is a materially different ability. No spec versions are present; the body does state the principal voltage thresholds.

comparisons.objective: Choose fitting tweezers and peel protective film while stabilizing its carrier, versus commission a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool selection, tweezer pinch, deformable peeling, bimanual holding, and tool return versus rigid hex-tool engagement, rotary adjustment, torque locking, and cycle inspection.
comparisons.success_condition: Film fully removed, carrier controlled, film laid outside, and tools returned versus two safe damped stops with retained setting.
comparisons.reason: This validated deformable peeling task does not test adjustable damping or fastener retention. No spec versions are present; holder-placement tolerances and final peel threshold are not fully numeric in the body.

comparisons.objective: Identify and open the correct junction box, free a cable, reclose it, and extract the cable, versus commission a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Selective lid manipulation and cable extraction versus precision tool insertion, fine rotation, locking torque, and dynamic feedback tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Only the containing box opened, then closed, with the entire cable released into the tray versus two safe stopping cycles and a passed lock-retention test.
comparisons.reason: Opening/reclosing and extraction are different from calibration and impact control. No spec versions are present; the short body omits numeric lid, cable, and tray thresholds.

comparisons.objective: Order, orient, and insert four tape cartridges, versus commission a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Barcode reading, regrasp/handover for orientation, slot alignment, insertion, and release versus hex-tool engagement, collar tuning, relocking, and repeated cycle assessment.
comparisons.success_condition: Cartridges 1–4 correctly ordered, label-out, upright, flush, and untouched for one second versus two safe damped stops and retained collar position.
comparisons.reason: This tests semantic sequencing and repeated keyed insertion, not dynamic calibration. No spec versions are present; 'flush' and orientation tolerances are not quantified in the body.

comparisons.objective: Remove and stow all remove-before-flight items, versus commission a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Recognize, extract, transport, and bag three safety items versus precision tool use, adjustment, torque locking, and guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: All three items removed from the aircraft and placed in the kit bag, with none left as debris, versus two safe stops and stable adjustment.
comparisons.reason: The task is checklist completion and extraction, not commissioning. No spec versions are present; the body lacks numeric extraction, bag-containment, and release tolerances.

comparisons.objective: Sequence dock-line handling so engine thrust springs a boat clear, versus tune and lock a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed multi-line release, retention, and retrieval around an externally driven boat versus small-tool alignment, fine rotary control, locking, and impact-response iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Three lines aboard before engine action, one bow spring retained until the stern clears, then all four aboard versus two safe carriage stops and post-lock stability.
comparisons.reason: Both interact with dynamic response, but line sequencing under thrust is not damping calibration. No spec versions are present; the body omits clearance, line-placement, and timing tolerances beyond the 30 s/10 s schedule.

comparisons.objective: Pull an extinguisher pin, read its gauge, and file a condition report, versus commission a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Linear pin extraction, gauge interpretation, and tag placement versus recessed hex-key use, collar adjustment, torque locking, and iterative guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Pin displaced at least 2 cm and tag within 2.5 cm of the correct pad versus two safe damped stops and acceptable post-lock drift.
comparisons.reason: Gauge-based inspection and reporting do not test mechanical response calibration. No spec versions are present, though the body gives the main scoring thresholds.

comparisons.objective: Pull an extinguisher pin, read its gauge, and file a condition report, versus commission a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Linear pin extraction, gauge interpretation, and tag placement versus recessed hex-key use, collar adjustment, torque locking, and iterative guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Pin displaced at least 2 cm and tag within 2.5 cm of the correct pad versus two safe damped stops and acceptable post-lock drift.
comparisons.reason: This record duplicates pr-1241, but remains distinct from the candidate because it tests inspection/reporting rather than calibration. No spec versions are present, though the body gives the main scoring thresholds.

comparisons.objective: Select and place nail plates on studs whose holes violate a depth rule, versus commission a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Visual measurement, rule-based selection, plate alignment, flat placement, and release versus tool insertion, counterholding, fine adjustment, locking, and dynamic testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Plate every and only stud with hole edge under 31.75 mm from the face, centered and flat, then release versus two safe carriage stops and retained adjustment.
comparisons.reason: This tests measurement-driven protective placement, not adjustable machine dynamics. No spec versions are present; centering and flatness tolerances are not quantified in the body.

comparisons.objective: Match leader and follower poses before enabling teleoperation, then steer around an obstacle, versus commission a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pose matching, safe enable sequencing, and continuous leader-arm path control versus hex-key engagement, collar tuning, torque locking, and response-based cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Follower avoids the glass and reaches the green dot after safe pose matching versus two safe physical stops and a lock-drift witness test.
comparisons.reason: Safe enable sequencing is shared only generically; the core ability is teleoperation path control rather than mechanical calibration. No spec versions are present, and the sparse body omits pose, clearance, target, and timing thresholds.

comparisons.objective: Stack three eccentric-weight bars in order and leave the stack balanced for 20 seconds; no damper commissioning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual stacking and balance management, not recessed-key engagement, collar adjustment, locking, or impact tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Independent standing stack; detailed stability tolerances are missing, but the goal is clearly unrelated to repeated carriage-stop behavior.
comparisons.reason: Tests balance construction rather than adjustment and validation of a shock absorber.

comparisons.objective: Start a pendulum and brake it on its third swing while stabilizing its stand; no mechanical damping adjustment.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual stand holding, timed release, swing counting, and button pressing; shares control actuation and observation only, not key/collar/setscrew work.
comparisons.success_condition: Brake once on the third return, avoid touching the moving bob, then withdraw; numeric timing tolerance is not stated.
comparisons.reason: The tested ability is temporal interception of oscillation, not iterative tuning and physical locking of a damper.

comparisons.objective: Extract a robot-assembly spacer using a pusher; no adjustable component is commissioned.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool-assisted pushing and extraction rather than loosening, fine rotary adjustment, relocking, and dynamic-response tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: The body references detailed contact checks elsewhere but does not reproduce them; spacer extraction remains clearly different from two validated impact cycles.
comparisons.reason: Different mechanical operation and outcome despite both being maintenance-like tool tasks.

comparisons.objective: Transfer a loaded tray and two tins to a shelf before withdrawing support.
comparisons.physical_skill: Load-preserving tray transport and hand withdrawal, not tool insertion, threaded locking, or iterative damping adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Tray and tins must remain together; exact containment and placement tolerances are missing.
comparisons.reason: Tests supported transport rather than shock-absorber commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Remove a corrugated insert and hand three supply boxes through a partition to clean storage.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cross-partition bimanual handovers and material segregation, not precision tool use or force-limited locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Boxes reach the clean shelf and cardboard stays on the dirty side; exact shelf tolerances are not given.
comparisons.reason: Tests constrained logistics and contamination-zone compliance, not mechanical adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Place four parcels into the smallest compartments they fit.
comparisons.physical_skill: Size-based allocation, parcel transport, and central handover; no fine rotary adjustment or fastener manipulation.
comparisons.success_condition: Each parcel occupies its smallest viable compartment; full size and fit thresholds are referenced but absent from the record body.
comparisons.reason: Tests packing allocation and handover, not commissioning from dynamic impact response.

comparisons.objective: Shelve cartons upright and front-facing while separating look-alike drugs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Carton reorientation, pocket insertion, and rule-aware placement, not key engagement, collar tuning, or torque control.
comparisons.success_condition: All cartons upright/front-facing and look-alikes nonadjacent; exact pose tolerances are missing.
comparisons.reason: Tests constrained shelving and semantic separation rather than damper adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Stand a calibration board in a holder facing a camera.
comparisons.physical_skill: Board grasping, orientation, and holder insertion; insertion is a generic shared primitive, without unlocking or dynamic tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Board must be in the holder and camera-facing; numeric pose and seating tolerances are missing.
comparisons.reason: Tests fixture placement and orientation, not adjustment and locked performance validation.

comparisons.objective: Pick six good packs from a moving belt into case cells while rejecting cracked packs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fast bimanual conveyor interception, classification, and packing, not fine tool alignment or force-controlled locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Six good packs must be cased before the red line and two cracked packs allowed through; cell and deadline details beyond the stated cadence are missing.
comparisons.reason: Tests high-throughput sorting under motion rather than iterative damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Map an isolated two-wire harness using four probe measurements and record PASS, CROSSED, or OPEN.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual spring-probe alignment/compression and electrical diagnosis, not collar rotation, setscrew manipulation, or impact-response adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Four valid contact-qualified measurements and the correct verdict; exact compression and alignment thresholds are missing.
comparisons.reason: Although both use precision tool contact and diagnosis, the tested physical mechanism and success outcome differ meaningfully.

comparisons.objective: Quench two aluminium fittings before a deadline while keeping a steel fitting dry and off the bench.
comparisons.physical_skill: Simultaneous bimanual hot-part transport and liquid placement, not adjustment, locking, or controlled impact testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Aluminium submerged by 6.0 seconds and retained there; steel never enters water and no hot part touches the bench.
comparisons.reason: Tests deadline-constrained material handling with irreversible safety rules.

comparisons.objective: Remove a rocking deck board, discard the pebble, and reinstall the board flush.
comparisons.physical_skill: One arm levers/holds the board while the other grasps it, followed by constrained reinsertion; no precision key/collar operation or response tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Pebble in bucket and board restored flush; numeric flush tolerance is missing.
comparisons.reason: Tests cooperative levering and board removal/reinstallation, not damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Connect each server's two power cords to different power strips.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated plug routing and socket insertion with cross-reaches, not fastener unlocking, fine adjustment, or witness-torque testing.
comparisons.success_condition: All six plugs inserted and every server split across PDU A and B; insertion-depth tolerances are missing.
comparisons.reason: Tests redundant power topology plus connector insertion rather than adjustable shock absorption.

comparisons.objective: Move five salmon pieces to a plate without robot-food contact by manipulating a board and knife.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual board positioning, stabilization, and tool sweeping; shares stabilization only, not precision locking or iterative tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Each piece reaches the plate and any robot-food contact zeros the score; spill/loss and plate-boundary tolerances are not detailed.
comparisons.reason: Tests indirect food transfer and hygiene constraints.

comparisons.objective: Put only dog-safe snacks into a bowl.
comparisons.physical_skill: Semantic selection and ordinary pick-and-place, not mechanical adjustment or force-controlled tool use.
comparisons.success_condition: Safe items belong in the bowl and toxic items must be excluded; exact placement and contamination rules are missing.
comparisons.reason: Tests safety knowledge expressed through sorting, not a different version of damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Serve one food to each guest without giving meat to the vegetarian guest.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rule-aware food assignment and placement, not fine insertion, rotary adjustment, locking, or physical-cycle diagnosis.
comparisons.success_condition: One item per plate with no meat for the VEG-marked guest; detailed pose and error conditions are missing.
comparisons.reason: Tests semantic allocation rather than mechanical maintenance.

comparisons.objective: Settle blackjack by paying 3:2 beside the winning bet and racking the busted bet.
comparisons.physical_skill: Chip counting, stacking, transport, and bimanual handover, not tool seating or damper tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Place three payout chips within 2 cm beside the untouched two-chip bet and rack the busted bet; capping or breaking the bet zeros the score.
comparisons.reason: Tests arithmetic and rule-constrained chip manipulation.

comparisons.objective: Pack a lunch so yogurt and sandwich are adjacent to a flat ice pack.
comparisons.physical_skill: Constrained object packing and orientation, not threaded unlocking, collar rotation, or dynamic-response iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Ice pack flat; yogurt upright and sandwich flat, each within 5 mm of it; perishables placed away from it invalidate the score.
comparisons.reason: Tests spatial packing under food-safety adjacency constraints.

comparisons.objective: Place cups on mats with contrasting tones.
comparisons.physical_skill: Visual matching and stable cup placement, not precision tooling, adjustment, or locking.
comparisons.success_condition: One cup per mat, upright, and contrasting; same-tone placement or any tip-over zeros the score.
comparisons.reason: Tests contrast-aware table setting.

comparisons.objective: Serve chopsticks lying on their rest and never upright in rice.
comparisons.physical_skill: Slender-object grasping and precise placement, not key insertion, fastener manipulation, or iterative impact tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Chopsticks must rest in the culturally appropriate pose; numeric pose tolerances and explicit failure boundaries are missing.
comparisons.reason: Shared fine placement is generic; the tested ability is culturally constrained utensil placement.

comparisons.objective: Stand a 1 kg filament spool up and slide it onto a holder rod until it reaches the stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual heavy-object reorientation, bore-to-rod alignment, and insertion; no unlocking, rotary tuning, or torque-limited relocking.
comparisons.success_condition: Spool threaded squarely onto a rod with 7 mm bore clearance and advanced to the stop; exact contact tolerance is missing.
comparisons.reason: Tests cooperative load alignment and shaft insertion, a meaningfully different ability from damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Sort four M8 and four M4 bolts into separate organizer compartments.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated fingertip pinching of small fasteners and size-based binning, not using a fastener as an adjustable lock or tuning a mechanism.
comparisons.success_condition: All silver M8 bolts left and all black M4 bolts right; detailed bin containment and damage criteria are missing.
comparisons.reason: Small-part manipulation alone does not overlap with the candidate's coupled unlock-adjust-test-lock procedure.

comparisons.objective: Release a loaded spring platform under control and store its retaining bar.
comparisons.physical_skill: Controlled stored-energy release and bar removal/placement, not recessed-key engagement, collar adjustment, or iterative damping calibration.
comparisons.success_condition: Controlled release and retained-bar storage are required; the record says numerical rules exist elsewhere but does not include release-rate or safety thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Both concern dynamic safety, but one controls a one-time spring release while the candidate tunes and locks repeated impact absorption.

comparisons.objective: Insert a rigid retaining fork into a shaft groove while stabilizing the fixture.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual fixture stabilization and tight side insertion; shares alignment/insertion generically but lacks rotary adjustment, threaded unlocking, and dynamic tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Both fork tines pass the shaft center, with partial lift credit requiring measured rise; exact groove clearances and rise threshold are absent.
comparisons.reason: Tests retainer installation, not adjustable damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Load and center a wafer on a spin-coater chuck using tweezers and an aligner while holding the lid.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool changes, edge-only wafer pinching, aligner docking/extraction, and sustained bimanual lid support; not fastener unlocking or damping adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Wafer centered on the 24 mm chuck within 0.5 mm, aligner removed, lid closed, and no gripper/top-surface contact.
comparisons.reason: Tests contamination-safe precision handling and centering, a different compound ability from impact-response tuning and lock retention.

comparisons.objective: Regulate a pendulum to a one-second period by repeated observation and bob repositioning; candidate commissions a robot-axis damper for safe repeatable stopping.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pendulum timing and sliding/repositioning a bob versus hex-key setscrew engagement, collar rotation, counterholding, relocking, and guarded impact cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: One-second free-swing period versus two ≥0.85 J stops within velocity/stroke limits, without bottoming, rebound, overload, or setting drift. Pendulum record lacks a numeric tolerance and detailed damage rubric.
comparisons.reason: Both use observation-driven adjustment, but they test different dynamics and manipulation: changing pendulum geometry versus unlocking, tuning, and mechanically retaining an impact damper.

comparisons.objective: Place two light gates astride an air track 200 mm apart; candidate tunes and locks a shock absorber from measured impact behavior.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fixture placement and spatial measurement versus recessed hex-key insertion, bimanual counterholding, fine collar adjustment, and torque-limited locking.
comparisons.success_condition: The record states 200 mm separation but omits tolerance, alignment, stability, and damage criteria; candidate requires two safe, repeatable dynamic stops within explicit energy, velocity, stroke, and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Static sensor placement does not test adjustment of a retained damping mechanism or validation through physical impact cycles.

comparisons.objective: Extract four metal fragments from beside a movable artery without injuring it; candidate commissions an industrial-axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Precision grasping and collision avoidance in a confined wound versus tool insertion, collar tuning, counterholding, locking, and machine-cycle actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Fragment removal with artery-contact penalties and zero on severe disturbance versus two bounded stopping cycles with no bottoming, overload, rebound, drift, or unsafe energized adjustment. Exact fragment-clearance thresholds are not supplied.
comparisons.reason: The objectives, contact risks, manipulated mechanisms, and terminal states are meaningfully unrelated despite both requiring careful contact control.

comparisons.objective: Use a rod through a narrow port to knock down hidden pegs without loading loose port edges; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Remote pivoting and constrained rod manipulation versus hex-key seating, bimanual stabilization, fine rotary adjustment, relocking, and dynamic testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Three pegs knocked down without disturbing port posts; detailed force/displacement thresholds are missing. Candidate requires two safe stops under explicit energy, velocity, stroke, rebound, and retention criteria.
comparisons.reason: Remote manipulation through a fulcrum-like port does not test commissioning or retention of an adjustable energy absorber.

comparisons.objective: Triangulate a buried corner iron from witness tapes and stand a stake on it; candidate commissions a robot-axis shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tape interpretation, hidden-location inference, and stake placement versus tool engagement, counterholding, collar rotation, locking, and guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Stake released upright on the recovered iron; localization tolerance and stability duration are absent. Candidate requires two quantified non-bottoming stops and post-lock retention.
comparisons.reason: Survey localization and placement exercise a different tested ability from mechanical damping adjustment and dynamic verification.

comparisons.objective: Strike a cue ball so a red ball enters a goal while respecting a reach line; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool pickup, aimed impulsive striking, and indirect ball control versus recessed-tool alignment, controlled collar rotation, counterholding, and bounded tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Red ball reaches the goal without hand/stick line fouls or pushing shortcuts; geometric tolerances are not stated. Candidate requires two repeatable safe impacts within explicit operating limits.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve impact physics, cue striking tests impulse direction and indirect aiming, not adjustment and retention of an impact-absorbing mechanism.

comparisons.objective: Raise a floating tag by dropping sinking slugs into water, then retrieve it; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated slug grasping, tube insertion, and float retrieval versus hex-key insertion, bimanual counterholding, fine collar tuning, locking, and cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Tag removed after water displacement, with cork-only and direct-reach shortcuts rejected; spill and exact clearance thresholds are unspecified. Candidate uses quantified energy, velocity, stroke, rebound, overload, and drift gates.
comparisons.reason: Fluid-displacement planning and retrieval do not exercise adjustable damping, fastener retention, or impact-response tuning.

comparisons.objective: Take manual blood pressure by inflating a cuff and controlling deflation while auscultating; candidate tunes an industrial shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pump operation, valve metering, and sustained stethoscope placement versus hex-key engagement, collar rotation, counterholding, relocking, and guarded impact testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Inflate above 160 mmHg and deflate past 100 mmHg at 2–4 mmHg/s while listening, then release equipment; candidate requires two safe, repeatable non-bottoming stops and retained setting.
comparisons.reason: Both regulate a physical response, but the medical task tests simultaneous pressure metering and sensing rather than mechanical adjustment retention and collision-energy absorption.

comparisons.objective: Break an over-centre knee brace and fold a radiator panel onto rest pads; candidate commissions and locks a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Applying force at a linkage knee and controlling a folding panel versus tool insertion, bimanual counterholding, collar adjustment, setscrew locking, and cycle testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Panel stowed and released on pads; exact angle, load, damage, and hold thresholds are missing. Candidate has explicit operating-envelope, hard-stop, rebound, and drift criteria.
comparisons.reason: Releasing and folding an over-centre linkage does not test iterative damping adjustment or setting retention.

comparisons.objective: Spot a scripted bench presser, intervening only when a rep stalls; candidate commissions a robot-axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed human-motion monitoring, bar capture, and assisted lifting versus small-tool alignment, fine rotary tuning, counterholding, locking, and machine cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Avoid early interference, catch the sixth stalled rep before the chest, and assist to lockout; candidate requires two quantified safe stopping cycles and retained adjustment.
comparisons.reason: Reactive load assistance and timing around a person are separate from tuning and mechanically locking an energy absorber.

comparisons.objective: Pass a drill safely to a coworker's palm, handle first and chuck away; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual drill grasping, orientation, compliant placement, and coordinated release versus hex-key insertion, collar adjustment, counterholding, and torque-limited locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Drill rests correctly in the palm without handle grasp, unsafe pointing, collision, or excessive speed; numeric pose/force tolerances are absent. Candidate uses quantified impact and retention gates.
comparisons.reason: Safe object handover does not test retained mechanical tuning or repeated impact response.

comparisons.objective: Select the correct tool from a cluttered pile and hand it over handle first; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Semantic tool selection, clutter extraction, reorientation, and handover versus tool-to-fastener alignment, counterholding, fine collar rotation, locking, and guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct mallet handed over in the required orientation while other tools remain undisturbed; exact pose/contact thresholds are missing. Candidate requires two safe stops and post-lock drift control.
comparisons.reason: Cluttered retrieval and handover exercise selection and transfer, not damping commissioning or mechanical setting retention.

comparisons.objective: Remove a rock from beneath a high-centred rover and restore the rover to its wheels; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Supporting or manipulating a bulky rover while extracting an obstruction versus small-tool engagement, collar tuning, counterholding, locking, and impact cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Rover restored upright without dragging or dropping; the record supplies no numeric displacement, damage, stability, or hold thresholds. Candidate has explicit operating-envelope and failure gates.
comparisons.reason: Obstacle extraction and vehicle recovery do not test adjustment of a damping mechanism or empirical stopping-response tuning.

comparisons.objective: Release a capped catch, lift and rotate a swing handle, and leave an enclosure lid open; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequential catch release, handle deployment/rotation, and lid opening versus recessed hex-key insertion, counterholding, fine collar adjustment, relocking, and dynamic cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct lid exceeds 60° and remains hands-off for 20 seconds; candidate requires two quantified non-bottoming impacts with no overload, rebound, or setting drift.
comparisons.reason: Both include a retained rotary control, but the enclosure task tests access-latch sequencing and lid state, not parameter tuning from dynamic response or fastener-secured retention.

comparisons.objective: Store keys in the initially open drawer, close it, perform an intervening placement, then retrieve the keys using only that drawer.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual chest stabilization, drawer operation, object placement/retrieval, sequencing, and memory versus hex-key use, counterholding, collar tuning, locking, and cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Complete the ordered storage/retrieval sequence, never open another drawer, close the drawer, and return both arms; numeric drawer and placement tolerances are missing. Candidate uses explicit physical-response limits.
comparisons.reason: Long-horizon drawer sequencing and object memory do not test shock-absorber adjustment or dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Mount and aim two cardioid microphones as an ORTF stereo pair; candidate commissions a robot-axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Dual microphone mounting, spacing/angle alignment, and aiming versus recessed-tool insertion, bimanual counterholding, collar adjustment, locking, and impact testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Record gives no spacing, angle, aiming tolerances, fastening criteria, or stability duration beyond the ORTF label. Candidate requires explicit energy, velocity, stroke, rebound, overload, and drift compliance.
comparisons.reason: Audio-array geometric rigging is unrelated to empirical damping adjustment and setting-retention validation; missing ORTF rubric details do not create a plausible duplicate.

comparisons.objective: Withdraw an uphill sample rod hand over hand through shrouds without letting it roll back; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Alternating bimanual regrasping, continuous support, and constrained linear extraction versus hex-key seating, counterholding, fine rotary adjustment, locking, and guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Achieve 17.2 cm rod travel to the target band with guide-disturbance gating; candidate requires two repeatable safe impacts and retained collar setting.
comparisons.reason: Both demand bimanual coordination, but hand-over-hand extraction under gravity is a different core ability from precision adjustment, fastening, and dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Tip a full-width pan of sand evenly across all 12 riffle-splitter chutes; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual load balancing, level-lip control, continuous tipping, and granular-flow distribution versus small-tool insertion, collar adjustment, counterholding, locking, and machine cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Title/body imply even feeding of all 12 chutes, but omit distribution tolerance, spill limit, retained mass, and terminal pose. Candidate has explicit energy, velocity, stroke, impact, and drift criteria.
comparisons.reason: Granular pouring and level-pan coordination do not test adjustable damping or lock retention; missing splitter thresholds do not suggest duplication.

comparisons.objective: Experimentally choose a liner that prevents a glass sliding on a 20° rack, then deploy it and place the glass.
comparisons.physical_skill: Material testing, flexible-liner handling, glass placement, and release versus rigid tool insertion, collar rotation, counterholding, setscrew locking, and impact cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Glass remains on a selected gripping liner on the 20° rack; the record omits slip distance, dwell time, and damage thresholds. Candidate requires two quantified safe stops plus post-lock drift control.
comparisons.reason: Both use empirical trials to choose a setting/material, but friction-material selection and deformable placement are meaningfully different from tuning and securing a mechanical damper.

comparisons.objective: Trace a leaking coolant branch through crossing lines and close only its valve; candidate tunes and locks a robot-axis damper.
